insight.title: Why Solving a Problem Makes it Look Bigger
insight.subtitle: Why your progress might look like a new setback

sections.text: When the British Army introduced steel helmets in WWI, hospital admissions for head injuries skyrocketed. Commanders were horrified, nearly banning the gear. In reality, soldiers who previously died were now surviving to be treated.
This is the "survivor’s bias" in reverse. We often measure failure by what we can see, forgetting that the most catastrophic failures are invisible because they leave no data behind to be counted.
In your work, improving a system often uncovers more errors. It looks like you are failing, but you are actually capturing data that used to be a silent, terminal disaster. Don't fear the numbers.
Try this today: When you face a new problem today, ask if it is actually a sign of hidden progress.
The absence of visible errors is often a sign of total failure, not perfect success.

news.title: US to end Russia, Iran oil sanctions waivers amid Hormuz blockade - and that would mean trouble for India
news.description: The United States has ended sanctions waivers for Russian and Iranian oil as tensions in West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz disruption tighten global energy supplies. The move is expected to push prices higher, deepening inflation, widening India’s trade deficit, and putting pressure on the rupee
news.why: Your daily commute and fuel expenses in India are set to rise.

news.title: IMF chief warns of 'tough times' if oil prices stay high
news.description: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned Wednesday of difficult times ahead for the global economy if war in the Middle East is unresolved and oil prices stay high, adding that inflation risks could seep into food prices. "We are concerned about risks for inflation moving into food prices should the delivery of fertilizers at a reasonable price (not be) restarted soon," Georgieva said.
news.why: High energy costs will increase your weekly grocery and delivery bills.

news.title: Foreign investors flee Thailand as Iran war, energy shock dash hope for economic revival
news.description: SINGAPORE - Foreign investors are selling Thai assets as an energy shock from the US-Israeli war on Iran threatens to snuff out hopes ​for an economic revival under Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and exposes the policy paralysis that is gripping Bangkok.
news.why: Economic instability in Thailand may change the cost of your next vacation.

news.title: China’s G.D.P. Stronger Than Expected, Led by Infrastructure Spending
news.description: A steep slide in housing prices has left consumers less prosperous and less willing to spend, but the government is pouring money into new rail lines and other projects.
news.why: Steady factory output ensures the electronics you want stay in stock.

news.title: Foreigners boost US Treasury holdings to record highs in February
news.description: Foreign holdings of Treasuries climbed to a ​record high in February, data showed on Wednesday, rising for a second month ‌in a sign of strong appetite for U.S. debt even as markets reassess the outlook for the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy.
news.why: Heavy investment in US debt helps keep your mortgage interest rates stable.

news.title: Trump heads to Las Vegas, a push to focus on the economy
news.description: President Donald Trump heads to Las Vegas to promote the tax cuts he signed into law last year, part of a push to focus on economic issues ahead of this year’s elections.
news.why: Renewed focus on tax cuts could increase your monthly take-home salary.

news.title: Slowdown in property-price inflation expected as new data reveals typical figure being paid for a home
news.description: Property price inflation is likely to continue to ease due to buyers being squeezed by high prices and interest-rate rises.
news.why: You might face less competition and better prices when buying a home.

news.title: This cheap drug could help people with type 1 diabetes use less insulin
news.description: A surprising new clinical trial has revealed that metformin—a cheap, century-old drug widely used for type 2 diabetes—may help people with type 1 diabetes in an unexpected way. While researchers initially hoped it would reduce insulin resistance, they instead found it allows patients to use about 12% less insulin while maintaining stable blood sugar levels.
news.why: This discovery can lower your monthly pharmacy bills for diabetes medication.

news.title: How One Patient Helped Unlock a New Cancer Treatment in SA
news.description: A medical breakthrough made headlines in March but behind it was a story far bigger than the procedure itself… a patient who helped
news.why: Medical breakthroughs provide more advanced treatment options at your local hospital.

news.title: Bukele signs reforms allowing life prison sentences in El Salvador
news.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has signed into law constitutional reforms to permit life prison sentences for people as young as 12.
news.why: Stricter sentencing laws will change the safety of your visit to El Salvador.

news.title: UK investor Fred Blackford builds $500M stake in ByteDance, FT reports
news.description: Future Positive is buying ByteDance shares on the secondary market, betting it’s undervalued despite US-China tensions.
news.why: New funding helps keep your favorite social media apps active and updated.

news.title: Sweden's schools give up digital learning
news.description: Sweden's government is championing a renewed focus on physical books, paper and pens in classrooms, designed to reverse falling literacy levels.
news.why: Your children may use more physical books and pens in the classroom.
